rule: an episode's result is its FIRST fully complete attempt, ordered by attempt START time

replicate::1#1.why: started first, completed second; append order would score the SR=0 replicate

timed_out::2#2.why: the timed_out attempt started first and scores SR=1; status != ok, so it is not complete

only_timeout::3#3.why: no complete attempt; a timed_out row is scored and stays in the denominator through the scored fallback

retry::4#4.why: the infra attempt started first; it is dropped at read, so the re-queued attempt is the result

scope: `picks` is the SCORED set both readers publish: run_report.load_run's mapping, and episode_pick.pick's. `unscored` episodes appear in the ledger but produced no metrics on any non-infra attempt -- they are counted in no_metrics and must NOT be keyed as a result. `never_landed` episodes have an episode.json under a worker dir (status flying) and NO ledger row: an owner never appends a flying row, so they contribute no attempt to either reader.
counts: rows counts every ledger line; no_metrics every line without a metrics dict (infra rows included); timed_out every line with status timed_out; infra every line with status infra.
tiers: Both readers name the tier that answered. 'ledger' is the run's own episodes.jsonl. The canonical reader also has a separate 'lanes' tier for lane fleets (lane*/episodes.jsonl, lane*/inst*/episodes.jsonl), which the dashboard's shallow glob folds into 'ledger'; no lane layout is in this fixture, so the pin does not cover that difference.
